summary:
SPACE GRAVEYARD – Echoes of Exploration is an interactive web-based experience that explores the forgotten remains of human space exploration. As humanity continues to explore space, many spacecraft, landers, and rovers are left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Our project brings these forgotten explorers back into focus through an interactive digital atlas.

Users can explore 3D representations of the Moon and Mars, discover the locations of historical spacecraft and robotic missions, and access detailed information about each artifact through interactive markers and mission dossiers. The project also features a Deep Space section highlighting spacecraft such as Voyager, New Horizons, and Pioneer 10.

By presenting scientific and historical information through an immersive and accessible interface, SPACE GRAVEYARD raises awareness about the legacy of space exploration and the growing presence of human-made objects beyond Earth. It reminds us that even when a mission ends, its story continues.
details:
SPACE GRAVEYARD – Echoes of Exploration is an interactive web platform that allows users to explore the remains of human space exploration across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

The website begins with an immersive space-themed interface where users can select one of three exploration destinations: Moon, Mars, or Deep Space. In the Atlas section, users can interact with 3D planetary models, rotate and zoom into the surfaces, and discover the locations of historical spacecraft, landers, and rovers through interactive markers.

Selecting an artifact opens its details, including its mission background, location, historical significance, and related information. Users can also search and filter artifacts, compare selected missions, explore mission information through dedicated sections, and record discoveries in an Explorer's Logbook. The Deep Space section highlights spacecraft such as Voyager 1, Voyager 2, New Horizons, and Pioneer 10.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand. Instead of presenting information through ordinary text or static images, it allows users to explore planetary surfaces and discover the remains of past missions interactively.

Its intended impact is to:

  • Raise awareness about human-made objects left on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
  • Preserve the stories and historical significance of past space missions.
  • Encourage interest in astronomy, planetary science, engineering, and space exploration.
  • Help students and the general public understand the legacy of robotic and human exploration.
  • Promote curiosity about the future of space exploration and the long-term presence of human-made objects beyond Earth.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed as a web-based application using:

  • HTML5 – Structure and content of the website.
  • CSS3 – Styling, layouts, animations, and responsive design.
  • JavaScript – Interactive features, navigation, search, filtering, and application logic.
  • Three.js – 3D planetary visualizations and interactive globe features.
  • NASA resources – Mission information, historical references, and planetary exploration data.
  • Wikimedia Commons – Additional images and visual resources.
  • Google Fonts – Typography.
  • jsDelivr CDN – Delivery of external libraries and texture resources.
  • Browser Local Storage – Saving Explorer's Logbook entries locally.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of SPACE GRAVEYARD is its approach to presenting space exploration through the idea of a digital graveyard. Rather than focusing only on active missions and successful landings, it highlights the spacecraft and exploration equipment that remain behind after their missions end.

The combination of interactive 3D planetary models, artifact locations, mission dossiers, deep-space exploration, and a personal Explorer's Logbook transforms historical information into an exploratory experience. The dark, cinematic interface and space-inspired visual design help create an immersive environment.

Factors Considered During Development

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, historical relevance, accessibility, usability, and visual experience. We aimed to present information in a simple and understandable way while maintaining an engaging interface. We also considered responsive design so that the website could be explored on different screen sizes, and optimized interactive elements to make navigation smooth.

Overall, SPACE GRAVEYARD aims to show that space exploration does not end when a mission stops communicating or a spacecraft completes its task. The objects left behind are reminders of humanity's journey into space, and each one has a story worth discovering.
